A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with complete, readable main text and Appendix A. Their equations, tables, figures and experimental descriptions can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization experiments on six synthetic and six real-world benchmarks, surrogate prediction experiments, and computational timing results in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original optimization, surrogate prediction and timing results, including the appendix tables and figures.

M1.justification: The GP and GP-ARD procedures retain the same Matérn-5/2 kernels, UCB acquisition function, marginal-likelihood training and NUTS alternative. The new benchmark implementation attribution in Appendix A.3 does not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six synthetic settings and six real-world tasks: Mopta08, SVM, Rover, DNA, NAS201 and NN-Prune. Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain their task definitions and dimensionalities.

E2.justification: Tree UCB, RDUCB, HESBO, ALEBO, SaasBO and TURBO retain the same evaluated variants, and the surrogate-learning comparators also match. The newly cited Papenmeier et al. (2023) supplies implementation attribution, not an additional evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain 20 initial queries, 400 optimization steps for synthetic tasks and 300 for real-world tasks, plus 300 training and 100 test examples for surrogate learning. The new Appendix A.3 note identifies implementation provenance without reporting a changed protocol.

E4.justification: The ARD versus shared-length-scale comparison, MLE versus NUTS analysis, prediction-alignment analysis and optimization trajectories are retained. Section 4.2 and Figures 3–7 contain no added or removed analyses.

E5.justification: Both report ten runs for optimization comparisons and five runs with standard deviations for surrogate prediction. The violin-plot summaries, predictive uncertainty displays and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 3–6 and plotted results in Figures 1–7 match. For example, GP-ARD's Mopta08 test log likelihood remains 0.613 ± 0.156 in Table 3, and its per-step runtime remains 11.23 seconds in Table 4.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), including the GP predictive distribution and acquisition function, are unchanged. Appendix A.1 retains the same synthetic-function definitions; no mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about standard GP's high-dimensional optimization performance, robustness across function structures and computational advantages of MLE. The abstract's added code-access sentence does not change the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Both retain the interpretations concerning structural-assumption mismatch, potential information loss from imposed low-rank structure, and the limited practical benefit of NUTS for standard GP. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: v2 adds an experimental-code repository link to the abstract. Appendix A.3 newly states that the SVM and Mopta08 implementations were modified from the repository associated with Papenmeier et al. (2023). Existing hyperparameter and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Papenmeier, Nardi and Poloczek (2023), Increasing the scope as you learn: Adaptive bayesian optimization in nested subspaces, and cites it for benchmark implementation provenance in Appendix A.3. The main related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a code-access sentence, Appendix A.3 gains one implementation bullet, and the bibliography gains one entry. Otherwise the wording, terminology and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: The additions cause limited text reflow and spacing shifts, including vertical repositioning of Tables 3–4 and Figure 3 on page 11. All figures and tables retain their content, numbering, captions and display structure.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides a direct pointer to the authors' experimental code and clarifies the provenance of two benchmark implementations. These additions modestly improve reproducibility documentation and attribution while leaving the scientific evidence and conclusions unchanged. The linked repository's contents and functionality cannot be established from the supplied PDFs.
